newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Amplats group to form single listed entity.
newsitem.headline: Amplats group to form single listed entity.

text.p: Anglo American Platinum Corp Ltd (Amplats) said on Tuesday it was restructuring the group into a single listed entity, using Rustenburg Platinum Holdings Ltd (RPH) as the vehicle.
At the same time, the group is disposing of its diamond interests to De Beers Consolidated Mines Ltd and Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd for around 1.2 billion rand.
Amplats' unlisted foreign diamond trading companies are being sold for $194.5 million in cash and the South Africa ones for 309.8 million rand.

Amplats said that the restructuring -- which it first said it was considering in April -- would allow it to focus on its core business of mining and marketing platinum group metals, while at the same time helping it move down the cost curve.
The new structure would give unconstrained choice in developing new mining projects, enabling it to manage its asset base more effectively, the group said.

Following the restructuring, Amplats will become a wholly-owned subsidiary of RPH and Potgietersrust Platinums Ltd (PPRust) and Lebowa Platinum Mines Ltd (Leplats) will be 100 percent owned by Amplats and RPH.
As a result, the listings of the shares of Amplats, PPRust and Leplats on Johannesburg Stock Exchange and the listing of PPRust and Leplats on the London Stock Exchange will be terminated.
RPH will be renamed Anglo American Platinum Corp Ltd.
Subject to shareholder approval, the RPH shares held by Amplats are to be distributed to Amplats shareholders in the ratio of 24.096 RPH shares for every 100 Amplats shares held.
Simultaneously, RPH will issue RPH shares as follows:
- 46 RPH shares for every 100 Amplats held;
- 41 RPH shares for every 100 PPRust held;
- six RPH shares for every 100 Leplats held.
